title: AI is changing which journalists matter to PR
notes: Emphasis markup: [[word]] renders in the accent yellow. Use on two slides per set at most.

lines: AI answers now decide which journalists matter.

slides.headline: Comms teams are keeping score.
slides.deck: Muck Rack started handing out AI Visibility Badges in March. Cision shipped a dashboard in July. Both rank reporters by how often AI cites them.

slides.text: The overlap between the journalists PR teams pitch most and the ones AI cites most, per Muck Rack. The pitch list and the citation list are two different lists.

slides.headline: AI rewards [[topical]] authority over [[general]] authority.
slides.deck: Google says AI Mode searches run two to three times as long as regular ones. ChatGPT prompts average 23 words. A question that detailed finds whoever wrote about that exact thing.

slides.quote: “The nerds, in other words, are winning.”
slides.deck: SemiAnalysis became a go-to on chip export controls. STAT, Endpoints News and Fierce Biotech own health. Skift owns travel. Pete Pachal on the beat reporters AI trusts.

slides.headline: Going deep is no longer a career liability.
slides.deck: Citations peak in an article's first seven days. Steady beat coverage keeps you in the answer.

slides.headline: Your LinkedIn counts more than you think.
slides.deck: It is one of the most-cited sources in AI answers, and more than half of those citations go to members with fewer than 10,000 followers.

items: Block the training crawlers. Let the retrieval crawlers through.
Let reporters go deep. Authority tied to a byline can walk.
Track AI presence, but skip the leaderboard. Gawker tried that.

slides.text: AI scores may fade the way Klout did. The pull toward [[deep expertise]] over [[famous bylines]] is the part that lasts.

slides.question: Who is the specialist in your field that AI keeps citing?
